findings.issue: Index 14 keys Parosmia (“Distorção ou alteração qualitativa do olfato.”) for “O perfume … antes era floral, mas hoje sinto nele um cheiro azedo, mesmo usando o mesmo frasco.” The control offered (the same bottle) does not show that the odour is unchanged: a perfume kept in its bottle can really turn sour over time, and “azedo” is the usual lay word for that. findings.resolution: Passed. Index 3 states excess and an adapted habit, index 8 opposes the speaker's perception to that of the others present, and index 4 gives an explicit external comparison; in each the complaint is heightened smell and no other script term fits. Whether an explicit baseline is required, and whether “exacerbação” covers earlier detection as well as intensity, are answer-key choices a teacher should confirm before clinical approval. Index 9 (B018-01) is the case where the reviewer could not pass without that decision.

findings.issue: The same subgroup prints Cacosmia as “percepção de um odor fétido que não existe no ambiente.”. Three Parosmia utterances replace a familiar odour with an unpleasant one: burnt (index 10), smoke with “não há nada queimando na cozinha” (index 13) and fish (index 17). A student could answer Cacosmia. In the base inventory the Cacosmia context is marked withheld-pending-definition-adjudication, with the note that the source wording describes a foul odour without stimulus.

findings.resolution: Reviewer agrees with the Parosmia-only key. In all three the altered smell is tied to a stimulus that is present (the coffee, the freshly cooked rice, the cream being applied), which is the distinction the inventory records for Parosmia; the source reserves Cacosmia for an odour that does not exist in the environment. Index 13 is the closest call, because the perceived smoke has no source of its own; it passes because the smell is attributed to the rice and smoke is not described as foul. A teacher may prefer to avoid smoke/burnt qualities in Parosmia stories or to state the Cacosmia boundary explicitly.

findings.issue: Entries considered because strong smells commonly trigger them or share wording: APARELHO DIGESTÓRIO > Náusea (“enjoo ou vontade de vomitar.”), APARELHO NEUROLÓGICO > Cefaléia (“dor de cabeça”), APARELHO ENDOCRINOLÓGICO > Hipersensibilidade (“Hipersensibilidade a temperaturas ambientais”), APARELHO DIGESTÓRIO > Halitose and APARELHO URINÁRIO > Cor e odor da urina. Indices 1 and 5 describe avoidance (closing the cupboard, pushing the jar away).
findings.resolution: None is supported. No utterance in the twenty mentions nausea, vomiting, headache, dizziness or sneezing (checked by reading and by a word search). Avoidance behaviour is not nausea. Hipersensibilidade in the script is about ambient temperature, not smell. Halitose and urine odour concern the patient's own breath or urine, not what is described.

findings.issue: Index 2: “várias fileiras antes” for distance is imprecise. Index 6: “do corredor de entrada” can attach to the oranges or to where the speaker stands. Index 8: the speaker is the one cutting the lemon, yet says “sinto o aroma de longe”; “ninguém mais … reclama” is weaker than “ninguém mais sente”. Index 15: “acontece com essa fruta de verdade na minha mão” is unnatural patient speech. Index 19: “sem ter mudado o alimento” is stiff.
findings.resolution: None changes the term or opens another one, so the stories pass. Suggested polish for a later edit: 2 “a várias fileiras de distância”; 6 “do corredor de entrada já sinto o cheiro das laranjas”; 8 “Quando alguém corta limão na cozinha, sinto o aroma do outro cômodo …; ninguém mais acha o cheiro forte”; 15 “e a laranja está aqui na minha mão”; 19 “e a cebola é a mesma de sempre”.

findings.issue: All ten Hiperosmia utterances use forte/intenso/marcante or early detection, and all ten Parosmia utterances follow the pattern “X now smells like Y”; the technical terms never appear. Each group shares one stock rationale (story and evidence) and one stock alternativeAssessment sentence. Indices 5 and 17 spell out the Hiperosmia/Parosmia contrast inside the utterance (“não parecia outro cheiro, só muito mais intenso”; “não é que esteja mais forte, está diferente”), which makes those two easy.
findings.resolution: Within the stated rules (lay speech, one paragraph, technical term not given away). findings.issue: Every acceptedPathEvidence entry in content/batches/interrogatorio-next-02.json (all 200 stories, including the twenty reviewed here) declares definitionBasis “originalDescription”.
